[6/10, 13:20] Alexander John: Hi Omaa —

Something is shifting in how serious Abuja real estate brands approach content.

The brands that are starting to win aren't just posting better properties — they're creating content that directly addresses the fears buyers carry into every viewing. Fear of fraud. Fear of title issues. Fear of a brand that disappears post-payment.

One brand here in Abuja recently invested time into understanding this and restructuring how their team communicates with buyers. The shift was significant.

I created a personalised audit for Omaa Homes that looks at where your content stands on this — and where the gaps are. Quick breakdown and specific to you.

Worth sending across?
[6/16, 16:05] Alexander John: Quick question, Omaa.

When a diaspora buyer lands on Omaa Properties  page, what in your content immediately tells them, "These people won't disappear with my money?"

Most Abuja brands can't answer that clearly.

The truth is, diaspora buyers aren't just buying property—they're buying trust.

I recorded a short breakdown showing a gap I noticed on your page and how I'd fix it.

Want me to send it over?
[6/26, 17:06] Alexander John: Most real estate pages in Abuja are accidentally marketing to the wrong buyer — their content attracts people who want to negotiate the price down, not people who want to know if it is available. I looked at your page and I think that might be happening with your listings. The fix is not more content, it is a small shift in how the property is framed in the first three seconds. Would it be useful if I sent you a quick example of what that looks like done right?

Omaa, I'll be direct — I've sent a few messages and you haven't responded, which usually means one of two things: either the timing is off, or what I'm saying isn't landing as useful. Either is fair. 

I'm not trying to sell you something you don't need. But I did notice something specific about how your listings are framed that I think is quietly filtering out your most serious buyers before they ever reach out. 

If that's worth 60 seconds of your time, I'll send it — no pitch, just the observation. If you dont find it useful you can blacklist my number.

[23/06/2026, 12:01:16] ~Dr. Charles: How do you know I don’t get buyers ?
 [23/06/2026, 12:07:22] Alexander John: Fair question.

I don't know whether you get buyers or not.

What I do know is that when I reviewed the page, I noticed a few positioning patterns that often make it harder for serious buyers to identify why they should trust a brand or take the next step.

The breakdown isn't based on your sales numbers—it's based on what I observed from the content itself.

You may already be getting great results. The video is simply an outside perspective on areas that could potentially be strengthened.


[6/27, 14:35] Alexander John: Charles, one thing I've noticed in the Abuja luxury property market right now — diaspora buyers (especially UK and Canada-based) are actively looking, but they're doing a lot of due diligence from abroad before they ever reach out. 

The content that converts them is less about the property specs and more about trust signals: developer credibility, site progress, and social proof from people like them. 

Most pages aren't building that layer at all. I'm curious — is diaspora traffic something you're actively trying to attract, or is your current focus more on local buyers?
[6/30, 17:20] Alexander John: The shift I'm seeing in Abuja right now is that diaspora buyers are arriving better informed than ever — they've already done the AGIS search, priced the neighborhood, and shortlisted three developers before they send a single message. The brands they engage with are usually the ones that posted verification content, not just drone footage. I'm curious what your current content is built around — are you leaning more into trust-building material or is it still predominantly visual?

Saadatu here from DFQLABS 
I assume you are focused on closing out your Q3 targets for the current units. Are you still looking to refine your acquisition strategy for the next phase, or is the current flow working well enough for your goals?

leads.meetingPrepNote:
PROSPECT SUMMARY:
Gideon is the founder and sole decision-maker of Zaravani, a real estate company he is actively building into a multi-arm investment and education brand. He is visionary, articulate, and clearly invested in brand architecture — not just property sales.

COMPANY SUMMARY:
Zaravani is being built as an integrated real estate investment company combining education, legal advisory, brokerage, and property development, with a stated ambition to become "the Bloomberg of African real estate." The media and content arm is actively under construction — Gideon is building a YouTube brand framework right now, meaning DFQLabs is entering at the exact moment the content infrastructure is being designed, not retrofitted.

CONVERSATION TIMELINE:
Alex cold DM'd on approximately June 22 with a hook-strategy observation on Zaravani's IG content. Gideon replied warmly the same day. Alex promised to send a sample but missed the follow-through for a week. Gideon followed up on June 29, Alex apologised and delivered a content structure breakdown the same evening, then offered a free 30-day strategy. Gideon engaged substantively — tried a post change immediately, asked about YouTube, and shared Zaravani's full brand vision. Alex qualified Gideon as the decision-maker on the spot, then proposed a call. Gideon counter-proposed a physical meeting. Alex redirected to a qualifying call first. The call happened on June 30, went well — Gideon thanked Alex warmly, shared his office address unprompted, and expressed interest in meeting in person. Alex sent a relevant IG reel on July 1. Gideon engaged today (July 2), confirmed the reel was useful, forwarded it to his tech team, and asked what time they are meeting tomorrow. Meeting confirmed for 12pm on July 3 at Gideon's office in Mabushi.

PAIN POINTS IDENTIFIED:
– Content volume without conversion architecture: Gideon is already posting and has some concepts, but his content is not built around buyer psychology or a trust-building sequence — the hook gap Alex first identified was real and Gideon confirmed it by immediately trying to apply it.
– Building a media arm without a strategic content framework: He is designing the YouTube architecture himself without a proven framework for what actually converts or builds trust in the Abuja buyer market. This is a high-risk approach — a lot of effort could produce content that looks good but does not generate qualified inquiries or serious investor interest.
– Targeting investors without investor-specific trust triggers: Gideon's own messaging around "inspiring confidence" and "people investing wisely" signals investor-facing content, but nothing in the thread suggests the content currently addresses the specific fears that serious Abuja investors carry — off-plan risk, title anxiety, developer abandonment history, FX exposure for diaspora buyers.
– Fragmented execution: He has a tech guy, a brand vision document, and a YouTube framework in progress — but no evidence of a single coordinating content strategy that ties those pieces into a buyer journey.

LIKELY OBJECTIONS:

"I already have a team working on this / I can handle the strategy myself."
Rebuttal: What you are building is impressive precisely because it is multi-arm — but that scale means a fragmented content approach costs more than it would for a simpler brand. The question is not whether your team can execute, it is whether the strategy they are executing against is built on how Abuja investors actually make decisions, or on what looks good. Those are two different things.

"Let me finish the media architecture first, then we can talk."
Rebuttal: This is actually the ideal moment — not after. The architecture you are building right now will determine the content pillars, the episode formats, the trust signals, and the CTA structure for the next 12-18 months. Retrofitting a buyer psychology framework into a finished architecture is significantly harder than building it in from the start.

"What is the cost?"
Rebuttal: Do not quote the rate card until you understand the full scope of what they are building. Zaravani's ambition (YouTube, investor content, brand architecture, brokerage, development) is not a Starter-tier brief. Position pricing as a scoping question — "the right engagement depends on which arms of the business we are building content strategy for first" — and anchor against what a single cinematic property video or a monthly ad spend costs, not against a generic retainer.

BUYING SIGNALS:
Strong. Gideon confirmed he is the decision-maker unprompted and in clear terms ("It's my company"). He shared detailed brand vision and a confidential brand architecture document framing. He tried to apply Alex's first piece of advice immediately after receiving it. He shared his office address without being pressed. He forwarded Alex's reel to his tech team the same day. He is asking about meeting time with forward energy, not stalling. The warmth is consistent and genuine — "highest regards," "warm hands of friendship," "I hope to see you soon." This is a Warm-to-Hot prospect who is already mentally open to collaboration.

RECOMMENDED MEETING OBJECTIVE:
Walk out with Gideon's answer to one question: which part of the Zaravani content architecture does he want to get right first — and is he ready to start in July? The goal is not to pitch everything
